outcome: Primary suture of the external anal sphincter detection
cohort: The study included 146 puerperal women who underwent vaginal deliveries at Valme University Hospital.
finding: 3-dimensional transperineal ultrasound is a helpful and comfortable method for determining primary repair of the anal sphincter and establishing early sphincter injuries that go unnoticed during immediate post-partum.
mod_finding: The study highlights that anal sphincter injuries are common with vaginal birth and confirms the utility of 3-dimensional transperineal ultrasound for diagnosing these injuries after vaginal deliveries.
